about:
Texas Microelectronics Corporation (TxMC) operates from Houston, Texas, where it was established over three decades ago. The company remains privately held, though ownership details such as family or veteran status are not publicly disclosed.

TxMC specializes in designing and manufacturing high-temperature, high-reliability custom hybrid circuits and multi-chip modules. Its services span design consultation, manufacturing, design integration, and packaging solutions. The firm also offers a catalog of standard products including ASIC multi-chip modules, switching DC-DC converters, linear regulators, high-voltage power supplies, analog-to-digital converters, amplifiers, and memory devices, all rated for case temperatures up to 230 °C. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

The company serves the oil and gas, aerospace, aerial drone, geothermal energy, and communications sectors. Customers range from research-and-development programs to accelerated high-performance product development teams.

TxMC emphasizes a partnership model with clients, citing its ISO 9000:2015, AS9100, and ITAR certifications as foundations for quality and compliance. The ability to deliver reliable operation at extreme temperatures is presented as a core differentiator.

about:
Texas Precision Performance operates from Coleman, Texas, as a veteran- and family-owned business founded by racers with deep drivetrain experience. The company emphasizes its 25-plus years in the industry, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The shop specializes in professionally built custom third-member center sections for Ford 9-inch and GM 8.5/8.6 differentials, covering street, strip, and full-race applications. It also stocks a range of differential parts including Ford 9-inch rear-end gears, Chevy 12-bolt components, and 55-64 Chevy rear-end parts, while carrying brands such as Eaton, Motive Gear, Yukon Gear & Axle, and Strange Engineering. The business runs an online parts storefront alongside its custom assembly work.

Primary markets are racing, off-road, and street-car enthusiasts who need durable drivetrain components for high-performance builds, rebuilds, or replacement parts.

The company states it refuses to sell inferior parts despite competitive pricing, positioning its combination of racer insight and veteran discipline as a differentiator for customers seeking reliable custom assemblies.

name: Texas Semiconductor Technologies
old_description: Texas Semiconductor Technologies is a professional Dallas-based company providing sales and service for semiconductor manufacturing equipment across the globe.
about:
Texas Semiconductor Technologies (TST) was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, by John Getchell. The company began as a specialist in complete tool refurbishment, field service, and sub-assembly reconditioning for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, operating today from a 100,000‑square‑foot facility that includes a cleanroom.

TST maintains what it describes as the world’s largest inventory of semiconductor spare parts — over 122,000 items — along with more than 50 refurbished tools ready for sale, including Lam Research models such as the 9600, 9400, 4520i, and Alliance platforms. The company also stocks over 300 pumps, chillers, and generators. A team of 30-plus technicians handles system refurbishment, cleanroom repair, sub‑assembly repair (particularly Lam Research components), installation, process qualification, and global field service. All inventory is owned by TST and available for inspection at the Dallas facility.

The customer base spans semiconductor fabs and chipmakers worldwide that run Lam Research and other OEM equipment. TST’s repair capabilities focus on RF matches, generators, power supplies, load locks, harmonic arm drives, and similar sub‑assemblies, offering exchange and consignment programs to minimize tool downtime.

The company emphasizes cost savings over OEM pricing, rapid turnaround, and a 12‑month warranty on non‑consumable parts. Its founder notes that filling a niche in certified semiconductor repair has driven the business since its start, and TST positions itself as one of the few certified repair facilities in the world.

about:
Textile Graphics operates from McMinnville, Oregon. The company has been active in the promotional products industry for over 45 years, building a reputation in screen printing, embroidery, and promotional merchandising.

The business provides screen printing, embroidery, and promotional merchandising services, supported by company stores, showrooms, an art upload portal, and e-commerce fulfillment for online stores. Its catalog spans thousands of items, from stainless‑steel drinkware and challenge coins to safety tools and corporate apparel, all customized to client specifications. Long‑tenured staff — averaging more than 25 years with the company — handle production and design.

Textile Graphics serves a range of sectors, including insurance, law enforcement, safety, and general corporate markets. Concrete examples include challenge coins and apparel for police departments, safety tools and gloves for industrial clients, and branded merchandise for trade shows and golf tournaments. The company also supplies corporate gift programs for employee recognition.

The company emphasizes its 100% Customer Satisfaction Guarantee, fast delivery times, and a consultative approach that includes product research and design assistance. Its differentiators are rooted in employee longevity and a commitment to strong client relationships, which the firm says drive repeat business and referrals.

name: Tezzaron Semiconductor Corporation
old_description: TSV-free 3D: Stacks the size of a single die. Better by design.
about:
Tezzaron Semiconductor Corporation is headquartered in Naperville, Illinois. The company entered the spotlight in 2004 when it demonstrated the world's first successful wafer-stacked 3D integrated circuits with through-silicon interconnects, including microprocessors, sensors, and SRAM devices. While the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the firm has since collaborated with dozens of customers to develop custom 3D-ICs for both prototyping and commercial production.

Tezzaron's core offering is its Di3D technology, a transistor-level 3D integration platform that combines wafer bonding, proprietary SuperContacts®, dis-integrated architectures, and BiSTAR® programmable self-test. The company handles the full development flow: adapting design tools, rewriting floor-planning rules, inventing and fabricating new structures, and creating novel test techniques and circuits. This end-to-end capability enables high-density, high-speed vertical interconnects in a footprint the size of a single die.

The technology targets high-performance semiconductor applications, including microprocessors, sensors, and memory devices. Tezzaron has participated in multiple multi-project wafer (MPW) runs for 3D-IC prototypes, partnering with organizations such as CMP (Circuits Multi Projets) in France. Its customer base spans companies seeking custom 3D-IC solutions for prototyping and volume commercialization.

Tezzaron was founded on the premise that conventional scaling had reached its limits and that a radical redesign of semiconductor component development was necessary. The company states that its approach "changes everything" about 3D integration, aiming to build a Di3D™ ecosystem of partners and licensees where the high-performance world can raise the bar for density and speed.

about:
The 49th Supply Co. operates from Anchorage, Alaska, where it runs a brick-and-mortar store alongside an e-commerce site. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company sells premium outdoor apparel and lifestyle goods under its own label, including hoodies, T-shirts, long-sleeve tees, hats, and accessories for men, women, and children. Product lines are organized into collections such as Wildflower, Classic, and a dedicated hat assortment. Orders over $150 ship free, and the storefront is open Monday through Saturday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.

The brand targets outdoor enthusiasts, local residents, and visitors to Alaska, with designs that reference Alaskan landmarks and culture. The website also publishes a local field guide and promotes community pop-up events, such as an R&B and boba gathering at a nearby coffee shop.

The company emphasizes its Alaska roots and community engagement as differentiators, combining retail with localized content and events.
